subject: Communication
title: Internal Storytelling: Culture as Narrative
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Internal Storytelling: Culture as Narrative.

hook.text: At Amazon, meetings start by reading a 6-page narrative memo in silence. No PowerPoints allowed.

buildup.text: Jeff Bezos banned slides because they hide weak thinking. Narrative forces clear, connected reasoning.

discovery.text: Internal stories — founding myths, hero employees, legendary failures — define company culture more than any handbook.

twist.text: Organizations without shared stories fracture. People need narratives to understand 'why we do things this way.'

climax.text: The best leaders are storytellers: they narrate where the company came from, where it's going, and why it matters.

punchline.text: Culture isn't rules. It's the stories people tell each other.

quiz.question: Why did Jeff Bezos ban PowerPoint at Amazon?
options: Because narrative memos force clearer thinking

details.summary: Organizational culture is built on shared stories more than policies or values statements. The stories employees tell about founders, crises, and defining moments shape behavior far more powerfully than any handbook. Culture is what stories get told and retold.
details.whyItMatters: Leaders who understand that culture is narrative can shape it deliberately. The stories you amplify become the behavioral norms your organization follows.
takeaways: Organizational culture is transmitted through shared stories
War stories about overcoming challenges define team identity
Leaders shape culture by choosing which stories to amplify

faq.question: How do internal stories shape employee behavior?
faq.answer: Stories about what gets rewarded, punished, and celebrated communicate actual values more clearly than any mission statement. If the famous company stories feature people who took risks, risk-taking becomes normal. If they feature people who played it safe, caution becomes the norm.

faq.question: How can leaders use storytelling to change company culture?
faq.answer: Identify and amplify stories that exemplify desired behaviors. Share them in meetings, all-hands, and onboarding. Create rituals around storytelling. When you see the behavior you want, turn it into a named story that gets retold. New stories gradually replace old cultural narratives.
